messages.subject: Item Information Plot
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm trying to select a subset of items from a 47-item physics conceptual inventory based on item information and have two questions:
1) is there a way to plot all item information curves in one plot for comparative purpose?
2) is there a statistical test to select the best x items?

Thank you, and happy holidays!
Karen

On Wed, Dec 18, 2019 at 1:16 PM KarenW <kdw...@stanford.edu> wrote:
Hi Phil,

I'm trying to select a subset of items from a 47-item physics conceptual inventory based on item information and have two questions:
1) is there a way to plot all item information curves in one plot for comparative purpose?

> plot(mod, type = 'iteminfo') 

should do the trick. plot() in mirt's convention is to plot the whole model object, in which case the set of all item plots constitutes the whole test.
2) is there a statistical test to select the best x items?

Can you define what you mean by 'best' items? That can be interpreted in many ways. 

Phil

Thank you, and happy holidays!
Karen

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: Re: Item Information Plot
parts:
It looks like a typo in your code plot(mod, type = 'iteminfo') 
Try this:
 itemplot(model, 1, type = "trace") # ICC for item 1
 itemplot(model, 1, type = "info")  # TIF - Test Information Function item 1
 plot(model, type = "trace") # ICC for all items on one page
 plot(model, type = "info")  # TIF for all items
 plot(model, type = "score") # TCC - Expected total score curve for all items

And you can use itemfit and personfit, fscores and coef to evaluate other relevant statistics/parameters

Cheers,

Guido
